entities.summary:
Annibale di Ceccano, born Annibaldo Caetani di Ceccano (died July 25, 1350), was a prominent Italian Cardinal who served the Avignon Papacy during a pivotal era of its consolidation. Hailing from the powerful Caetani family, which had previously produced Pope Boniface VIII, Annibale's career exemplifies the intricate interplay between noble lineage, ecclesiastical ambition, and papal administration in the 14th century. His influence extended across the Curia, particularly through his roles in papal finance and diplomacy, making him a significant, albeit often overlooked, figure in the political and cultural landscape of the High Middle Ages. His architectural patronage in Avignon, the seat of the papacy at the time, left a lasting physical legacy.

Elevated to Cardinal-priest of San Pancrazio by Pope Benedict XII in 1338, Annibale quickly became an influential member of the Sacred College. He served as Camerlengo of the Sacred College from 1342, overseeing significant financial and administrative aspects of the papacy. His diplomatic acumen was recognized through his appointment as papal legate to the Kingdom of Hungary in 1344 and later to the Kingdom of Naples in 1345, where he played a crucial role in mediating disputes and asserting papal authority in complex regional politics. These legations were not merely ceremonial but involved active negotiation and the assertion of papal prerogatives in volatile European territories, demonstrating his practical administrative capabilities.
